about.intro: Hairland is a Prague-based shop specialising in the sale of premium natural hair extensions. We offer natural hair from direct import and arrange custom processing to our customers' exact specifications.
about.storyText1: Hairland was born from a simple idea — to provide Czech women and hairdressers access to truly high-quality natural hair at fair prices, without unnecessary middlemen. about.storyText2: We personally inspect and sort every shipment by quality, length and colour. This is not mass production — we treat every kilogram of hair individually. That is why we stand behind the quality of our hair.
about.importText: We import hair directly from collectors and processors in more than 8 countries. No middlemen, no unnecessary markups.
about.processingText: We sell unprocessed hair. If you need processing into clip-in, tape-in, keratin bonds, micro ring or wefts, we arrange it with a verified partner within 7 business days.
about.supportText: We communicate in Czech, Ukrainian and Russian. We advise on selection, weight and processing method. Free delivery across Prague.
about.valueQualityDesc: We sell exclusively 100% natural human hair with intact cuticle. We inspect every delivery by hand — no synthetic additives.
about.valueDirectImportDesc: Thanks to direct contacts with collectors, we offer significantly lower prices than competitors while maintaining the highest quality.
about.valueCustomProcessingDesc: We arrange processing to the required method (clip-in, tape-in, keratin, micro ring, weft) with a verified partner within 7 business days. Express in as little as 3 days.

terms.section2Text:
2.1. Ordering goods takes place through personal selection of hair by the buyer, via the order form on hairland.cz or by other agreed means (email, phone).

2.2. The purchase contract is concluded at the moment of order confirmation by the seller and payment of the agreed purchase price by the buyer.

2.3. In the case of custom processing (clip-in sets, tape-in strips, keratin bonds and other modifications), the contract is concluded at the moment of order confirmation and payment of a deposit of 100% of the purchase price.

2.4. The seller reserves the right to reject an order or B2B account registration without stating a reason.

2.5. For B2B registration (salon registration), access to the portal is subject to approval by the seller. The seller verifies whether it is a professional hairdressing salon or a business in the industry.
terms.section3Text:
3.1. All prices are stated in Czech crowns (CZK). For B2B customers (VAT payers), prices are stated excluding VAT unless explicitly stated otherwise. For end customers, prices include VAT.

3.2. Payment is made:
  a) in cash upon personal pickup,
  b) by bank transfer to the seller's account based on the issued invoice,
  c) by deposit for custom processing.

3.3. The invoice — tax document is sent to the buyer electronically by email or handed over upon personal pickup.

3.4. In case of late payment of an invoice, the seller is entitled to charge the statutory late payment interest.
terms.section4Text:
4.1. Hair in stock is available immediately upon personal pickup.

4.2. Custom processing (clip-in sets, tape-in strips, keratin bonds) is completed within 7 business days from order confirmation and payment of the purchase price.

4.3. Delivery of ordered goods across Prague is free of charge. Delivery outside Prague is possible by individual arrangement and subject to shipping costs.

4.4. The buyer is obliged to inspect the goods upon receipt — especially colour, length, quantity and overall condition of the hair. Later complaints regarding obvious defects (mismatched colour, length, visible damage) will not be considered if not reported upon receipt.

4.5. If the buyer refuses to accept the goods without valid reason, the seller is entitled to claim compensation for delivery costs.
terms.section5Title: 5. Nature of the goods — natural hair
terms.section5Text:
5.1. The subject of sale is natural human hair. It is a specific product whose properties (subtle variations in colour, texture and thickness) are due to its natural origin and do not constitute a defect.

5.2. The seller states the exact origin of the hair, quality category (Virgin, Premium, Standard) and available parameters (length, colour) for each product. These details are indicative — minor variations typical of natural material are not grounds for complaint.

5.3. The lifespan of the hair depends on the application method, maintenance and products used. The seller is not liable for reduced lifespan caused by improper care.
terms.section6Text:
6.1. The buyer has the right to complain about goods if they exhibit quality defects that were not caused by improper handling, within 14 days of receipt.

6.2. Complaints must be made without undue delay by email to info@hairland.cz with a description of the defect, photo documentation and proof of purchase.

6.3. The seller will assess the complaint within 30 days of its submission.

6.4. IMPORTANT — A complaint cannot be accepted if the hair has been handled in any way after receipt, in particular:
  a) the hair has been applied by any method (keratin, tape-in, micro-ring, clip-in, sewing, other method),
  b) the hair has been prepared for application (tape attachment, creation of keratin bonds, cutting into strands),
  c) the hair has been washed, coloured, bleached, toned or chemically treated,
  d) the hair has been exposed to unsuitable products (sulphate shampoos, alcohol-based products, silicone oils unsuitable for hair extensions),
  e) the hair has been mechanically damaged (excessive brushing, unsuitable brushes, sleeping without protection),
  f) the hair has been heat-damaged (flat iron, curling iron without heat protection at temperatures above 180 °C).

6.5. Only unused, unapplied and unprocessed hair in its original condition as delivered to the buyer may be subject to complaint.

6.6. In the case of a valid complaint, the buyer is entitled to an exchange for defect-free goods or issuance of a credit note. The seller determines the method of complaint resolution.

6.7. The seller is liable for hidden material defects (e.g. inhomogeneous cuticle structure, incorrect direction of hair scales discovered only after application) even after application, within 30 days of receipt. In such cases, photo documentation and a report from the applying hairdresser must be provided.
terms.section7Text:
7.1. Returns are only possible for unused, unapplied and unprocessed hair in its original condition, within 14 days of receipt.

7.2. Returns must be arranged in advance by email at info@hairland.cz. Returns without prior arrangement will not be accepted.

7.3. The following cannot be returned:
  a) hair that has been handled in any way (see Art. 6.4),
  b) custom-made hair (clip-in sets, tape-in strips, keratin bonds),
  c) hair whose original packaging or labelling has been damaged.

7.4. If the conditions for return are met, the seller will refund the purchase price to the buyer's account within 14 days of receiving the returned goods.

7.5. The cost of returning goods is borne by the buyer.

offer.faq1q: How to choose the right hair extensions?

offer.faq3q: What extension methods do you offer?
offer.faq3a: We arrange processing for keratin, tape-in, clip-in, micro ring and weft extensions through a verified partner. Processing takes 5–7 business days.
offer.faq4q: Can I see the hair in person?
offer.faq4a: Yes — we come with samples directly to you in Prague for free. Just contact us and we'll arrange a time that suits you.
offer.faq5q: How long do hair extensions last?

complaints.title: Complaints policy
complaints.subtitle: Procedure for claiming purchased goods
complaints.section1Text:
1.1 This complaints policy governs the rights arising from defective performance for goods purchased in the online store hairland.cz, operated by Altro servis group s.r.o., ID 23673389, registered at Školská 660/3, 110 00 Praha 1 (hereinafter referred to as the "Seller" or "Hairland"). Contact for complaints: info@hairland.cz, +420 608 553 103.

1.2 The Seller exclusively sells unprocessed real human hair. The Seller does not process hair into clip-in sets, tape-in strips, keratin strands or other finished products, does not perform hair application and does not provide hairdressing services.

1.3 Based on individual agreement, the Seller may advise the Buyer on choosing an extension method or arrange processing or application by a third party. The Seller does not perform such processing or application and is not responsible for them. Defects in processing or application shall be claimed by the Buyer directly from the person who performed the work. Stylists listed on the Seller’s website are independent contractors.

1.4 The Seller is solely responsible for the quality of the supplied hair material in the condition in which it was handed over. The Seller is not responsible for its subsequent processing, application, modification, removal, or hair care after handover.

1.5 This complaints policy distinguishes two regimes based on the Buyer’s status:

Buyer — business entity (B2B): Stylist, salon, self-employed person or company purchasing within business activities (typically with a Company ID). Legal framework: § 2099–2117 of the Civil Code. The two-year period under § 2165 does not apply; Article A6.1 applies. The 14-day withdrawal right does not apply.

Buyer — consumer: A natural person purchasing outside of business activities. Legal framework: § 2161–2174b of the Civil Code + Act No. 634/1992 Coll. Statutory defect period: 24 months from receipt. The 14-day withdrawal right applies (§ 1829 of the Civil Code).

1.6 Entering a Company ID in the order is considered a purchase within business activities. A Buyer who enters a Company ID cannot subsequently exercise consumer rights.

1.7 By concluding the purchase contract, the Buyer confirms that they have read this complaints policy and the Hair Extension Care Guide, including the obligation to pass the guide on to the end client.
complaints.section2Title: A2. Product characteristics and acceptable deviations
complaints.section2Text:
2.1 The subject of sale is 100% human hair — a natural product of biological origin. It is not an industrially manufactured product with guaranteed piece-to-piece consistency. Minor differences between strands, shipments and individual hairs are a property of the material, not a defect.

2.2 The following deviations are not considered defects, provided they do not exceed the stated limits:

Shade compared to swatch or photograph — Slight tone deviation; photographs and monitors distort color
Strand / package weight — ± 5% of declared weight
Hair length — ± 2 cm; hair is not cut to a single line, ends are naturally layered
Texture — Slight waviness, varying thickness of individual hairs, different behavior after washing
Hair shedding — Occasional hair release during first combing and washing
Smell — Faint natural hair odor before first wash

2.3 Hair is supplied unprocessed, without modifications and without application. Any intervention after handover — processing into a set, application, cutting, dyeing, toning, washing, heat styling — is performed by the Buyer or a third party at their own responsibility. If processing was arranged by the Seller (Article A1.3), the Buyer shall claim its defects directly from the processor.

2.4 Light shades (platinum and light blonde) have inherently lower durability than dark ones. Faster drying of ends, lower strength and susceptibility to breakage in these shades is not a defect but a property resulting from lower pigment content and previous lightening.

2.5 Mild shedding of individual hairs up to 5% of volume per month with proper care is a normal consequence of use, not a defect.

2.6 The Seller recommends ordering a sample before ordering a larger quantity to assess shade and texture. Not ordering a sample does not establish the right to claim shade differences.
complaints.section3Title: A3. Mandatory inspection of goods before application
complaints.section3Text:
This is the key provision of the entire complaints policy.

3.1 The Buyer is obligated to inspect the goods immediately upon receipt and always before starting application. The inspection shall be performed on dry, unapplied hair: shade, length, weight, texture and packaging integrity.

3.2 Defects discoverable during this inspection — especially shade, length, weight, texture, packaging damage — must be reported before application. By applying, cutting, dyeing, washing or otherwise modifying the hair, the Buyer confirms that the goods meet the order in these properties.

3.3 Applied hair cannot be returned or exchanged due to shade, length or texture. Application makes the goods used and modified, and they cannot be restored to their original condition.

3.4 The Buyer — business entity is obligated to perform the inspection pursuant to § 2104 of the Civil Code as soon as possible after the transfer of risk of damage and to report discoverable defects without undue delay, no later than 3 business days from receipt. The Seller shall disregard later reports of obvious defects.

3.5 To document the condition of the goods upon receipt, the Seller recommends taking photographs of the unpacked goods before application. Without them, the assessment of shade or weight complaints may be evaluated against the Buyer.

3.6 Personal inspection before purchase. The Seller typically hands over goods in person and allows the hair to be inspected and compared in person before purchase. If the Buyer inspected the hair in person before purchase or upon handover, they cannot subsequently claim shade, length, texture or weight — i.e., properties they could have assessed during the inspection. The Seller keeps a written record of the personal handover and inspection confirmed by the Buyer.

3.7 Inspection at an intermediary. If personal handover by the Seller is not possible, especially for Buyers from other cities, the Seller may arrange an inspection of the hair at a cooperating person in the Buyer’s location. If the Buyer inspected the hair this way before purchase and confirmed that the shade, length and texture meet their requirements, such inspection has the same effect as a personal inspection under Article A3.6. Confirmation is sufficient in written or electronic form, including a message in an application.

3.8 Shipment without inspection. If pre-purchase inspection is not possible and the Buyer wishes to have the goods shipped, they bear the risk that the shade may appear different in reality than in the photograph. Shade deviation within the limits of Article A2.2 is not a defect in such case.

Method of purchase → Can shade and texture be claimed?
Personal handover and inspection → No — the Buyer saw and approved the goods
Inspection at intermediary with confirmation → No — same effect as personal inspection
Shipped without any inspection → Only if tolerances under Article A2.2 are exceeded

3.9 Hidden defects after application. A material defect that could not have been discovered during pre-application inspection — especially non-homogeneous cuticle direction or significantly uneven texture within a single delivery — can be claimed even after application. In such case, the Buyer is obligated to provide a written statement from the stylist who applied the hair, describing the discovered condition, and the Seller is entitled to request an expert assessment.
complaints.section4Title: A4. What constitutes a product defect — valid complaints
complaints.section4Text:
4.1 A defect is a condition that existed at the time of handover or resulted from properties of the material, not from use, application or care. The Seller will accept in particular:

• Incorrectly delivered goods — different shade, length, weight or number of strands than stated in the order and invoice.
• Significant shade difference compared to the binding sample or shade number in the swatch, exceeding the deviation under Article A2.2.
• Weight or length outside the tolerance stated in Article A2.2.
• Excessive hair shedding manifesting from the very beginning, i.e., during first combing and washing before application.
• Admixture of synthetic or animal fiber in material declared as 100% human hair.
• Chemical odor or visible silicone coating that is not removed after two deep-cleansing washes.
• Damage to goods during transport, reported within 2 business days of delivery with photo documentation of the packaging and contents.

4.2 A defect is also considered a condition where, with demonstrably proper care according to the Care Guide, the hair loses its normal functional properties substantially earlier than corresponds to the usual lifespan (Article A10). Such condition is assessed by the Seller individually; the Buyer is obligated to document the products and care routine used.

4.3 The Seller is not responsible for defects caused by processing of hair into clip-in, tape-in, keratin strands, micro ring strands or weft form, nor for defects in application. A crumbled keratin bond, non-holding tape, loose sewing or non-compliant weight of the processed set are defects of the processor’s work, not defects of the supplied material.
complaints.section5Title: A5. What is not a defect — grounds for complaint rejection
complaints.section5Text:
5.1 The Seller is not responsible for defects arising after the transfer of risk of damage to the Buyer as a result of use, modification, application or care. A complaint will be rejected particularly in the following cases:

a) Insufficient or no care
Extended hair is not connected to the scalp and does not receive natural sebum. Without supplementary nourishment, it inevitably dries out, breaks and matts. Therefore, the following conditions are not considered defects:
• not using a mask, leave-in conditioner or oil as specified in the Care Guide,
• washing with shampoos containing sulfates, alcohol, salt, or anti-dandruff shampoos,
• using products for oily hair or deep-cleansing products,
• insufficient brushing leading to matting at the bond area.

b) Heat damage
• straightening, curling or blow-drying without a heat protection product,
• using temperatures above 180 °C, especially repeated straightening of the same area,
• heat styling at the bond, keratin, tape or ring area,
• blow-drying on hot setting close to the bonds.

c) Chemical treatments
• bleaching, highlighting, use of products with peroxide or ammonia,
• dyeing to a darker or lighter shade without a prior strand test,
• dyeing or toning at the bond area,
• keratin straightening, perms, hair botox,
• any product that changes the hair structure.

d) Improper processing, application, modification or removal by a third party
• processing of hair into a set performed by the Buyer or a third party,
• hair application by a stylist or DIY, including inappropriate strand sizes, excessive tightening, incorrect curling iron temperature,
• damage to hair during removal, including use of an improper remover or mechanical pulling,
• cutting, thinning or texturizing that cannot be reversed.

The Seller is not responsible for the work of the stylist or processor, even if the Seller recommended or arranged them.

e) External factors and normal wear
• chlorinated water, sea water, sauna, solarium, prolonged sun exposure,
• sleeping with wet hair or without securing hair,
• friction against clothing, handbag or seatbelt along the hair length,
• gradual loss of shine and volume corresponding to the duration of use per Article A10.

5.2 A complaint about the appearance of hair filed after a longer period of use without documented care will be rejected. The Buyer is obligated to document that they provided care according to the Care Guide, particularly with a list of products used.

5.3 The Seller is entitled to reject a complaint if the claimed hair shows signs of damage that, according to expert assessment, is typical of heat, chemical or mechanical stress, regardless of the Buyer’s claims.
complaints.section6Title: A6. Deadlines for filing a complaint
complaints.section6Text:
6.1 Buyer — business entity

Obvious defects (shade, length, weight, damaged packaging, number of strands) — Within 3 business days of receipt, always before application
Hidden material defects — Without undue delay after discovery, no later than 6 months from receipt
Transport damage — Within 2 business days of delivery

After these deadlines expire, the right from defective performance is extinguished if exercised late (§ 2112 of the Civil Code).

6.2 Buyer — consumer

The consumer may report a defect within 24 months of receipt. If a defect manifests within 12 months of receipt, it is presumed that the goods were defective upon receipt. After this period, the burden of proof lies with the consumer. Articles A3 and A5 also apply to consumers — this is not a shortening of the statutory period, but a definition of what is not a defect.

6.3 Filing a complaint does not affect the Buyer’s obligation to pay the purchase price.
complaints.section7Text:
7.1 The Buyer shall file a complaint by email to info@hairland.cz or by submitting a completed complaint form.

7.2 The Buyer is obligated to provide the following with the complaint:

1. Proof of purchase — order number or invoice.
2. Description of defect — what the defect specifically consists of and when it manifested.
3. Date of application and method, name and contact of the stylist who applied the hair.
4. Photo documentation — overall view of the hair, bond detail and defect detail in daylight, without filters.
5. List of products used — shampoo, conditioner, mask, oil, heat protection, including names and brands. Failure to list products is grounds for rejection under Article A5.2.
6. Claimed goods — clean, combed and dry. For applied hair, the entire strand including the bond, not individual hairs. For unapplied hair, the complete package.

7.3 The Seller is not obligated to accept visibly soiled, odorous or unwashed goods for assessment, for hygienic reasons.

7.4 The cost of shipping the claimed goods to the Seller is borne by the Buyer. For accepted complaints, the Seller will reimburse the Buyer for these reasonably incurred costs. Shipments sent cash on delivery will not be accepted.

7.5 The Seller does not return claimed goods if the Buyer requested their disposal, or if the Buyer does not collect the goods within 30 days of notification after complaint rejection.
complaints.section8Title: A8. Complaint assessment and resolution deadlines
complaints.section8Text:
8.1 The Seller shall issue the Buyer a written confirmation of complaint receipt stating the date, content of the complaint and requested method of resolution.

8.2 Assessment is performed by visual and tactile inspection of the sample, and in justified cases by expert assessment by an independent expert or laboratory. The result of the expert assessment is decisive for complaint resolution.

8.3 Resolution deadlines

Consumer — Within 30 days of filing the complaint, unless the parties agree on a longer period
Business entity — Within 30 days of receiving the claimed goods; if expert assessment is required, within 60 days

8.4 The deadline does not run during the period when the Seller is waiting for documents under Article A7.2 that the Buyer has not provided. The Seller shall notify the Buyer of the need for supplementation.

8.5 The Seller shall notify the Buyer of the method of resolution by email and, in case of rejection, shall state the reason with reference to the relevant article of this policy, or with the conclusion of the expert assessment.
complaints.section9Title: A9. Methods of resolving an accepted complaint
complaints.section9Text:
9.1 Due to the nature of the goods, repair is not possible. An accepted complaint is resolved by:

• exchange for goods of the same type, shade and length, if in stock,
• a reasonable discount from the purchase price, if the defect is minor or the shade deviation can be resolved by a stylist,
• refund of the purchase price upon withdrawal from the contract, if there is a material breach of contract or if exchange is not possible.

9.2 The Buyer states their preferred method of resolution when filing the complaint. For the Buyer — business entity, the Seller determines the method of resolution, taking into account the Buyer’s request and the nature of the defect.

9.3 When refunding the purchase price for already applied hair, the duration and extent of use and the irreversible modification of the goods shall be taken into account. The Seller does not reimburse costs of processing, application, removal or repeated hairdressing service; these are borne by the service provider.

9.4 The Seller does not reimburse indirect damage, lost profit or harm incurred by the Buyer — business entity towards their clients.
complaints.section10Title: A10. Product lifespan and warranty scope
complaints.section10Text:
10.1 Statutory liability for defects is not a lifespan warranty or a promise that hair will retain its properties regardless of handling. It applies to defects that the goods had upon receipt.

10.2 Usual lifespan with care according to the Care Guide, which the Seller states as indicative:

Keratin strands — 3–6 months until repositioning, material can typically be repositioned 2–3 times
Tape-in strips — 6–8 weeks until repositioning, material typically 2–4 repositionings
Micro rings / nano — 2–4 months until repositioning, material typically 2–3 repositionings
Clip-in / hairpieces — 6–12 months with use several times a week

10.3 The stated values are indicative and do not constitute a warranty. Actual lifespan depends on washing frequency, heat styling, quality of care, physical activity and the growth rate of your own hair.

10.4 Gradual loss of shine, slight lightening of ends and volume reduction over time are signs of wear, not defects.

complaints.section12Title: A12. Withdrawal from contract within 14 days (consumers only)
complaints.section12Text:
12.1 Not every Buyer has the right to withdraw from the contract without stating a reason within 14 days. The Seller does not have a brick-and-mortar store; all goods are handed over in person or shipped. Therefore, the following regimes apply:

Personal handover to the Buyer — consumer → Yes — contract concluded outside business premises
Order on the e-shop or via Instagram with shipping → Yes — distance contract
Goods shipped after inspection at intermediary → Yes — inspection precludes shade claims (Article A3.7), but not the right to withdraw
Buyer — business entity (any method) → No — the right belongs only to consumers

12.2 Hygienic sealing of goods. Hair is delivered in a sealed package with a hygienic seal or security tape. It is goods that, for hygienic reasons, are not suitable for return after the package has been opened. If the consumer breaks the seal, the right to withdraw from the contract is extinguished (§ 1837(g) of the Civil Code). The Buyer is informed of this fact before concluding the contract, on the packaging and in the order confirmation.

12.3 Inspection and hygienic seal. Inspection of goods before purchase — both personal and at an intermediary — takes place on samples or in an unopened transparent package without breaking the seal. By breaking the seal, the Buyer confirms that they accept the goods in the condition in which they inspected them.

12.4 Only hair that is unused, unapplied, unmodified and unprocessed, in its original condition and original packaging, with an intact seal or marking, may be returned.

12.5 If the goods have been combed, washed, cut, dyed, processed into a set or applied, the contract cannot be withdrawn from — the goods are used and for hygienic reasons cannot be resold.

12.6 The Seller shall refund the purchase price within 14 days of the goods being returned, in the same manner as the payment was received. The cost of returning the goods is borne by the consumer.

12.7 Withdrawal under this article is a right distinct from a complaint. It cannot be used to return goods that ceased to be satisfactory only after use.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Answers to the most common questions about hair, extensions and our services
faq.q1: How to order hair at hairland.cz?
faq.a1: Choose hair in our e-shop, select the length and weight, add to cart and complete the order. If you need help choosing, we offer a free consultation — just contact us.
faq.q2: Can I try the hair in person?
faq.a2: Yes, we offer a personal consultation in Prague where you can inspect the hair, compare shades and try it on. The consultation is free and without obligation. More on the Hair Extensions Prague page.
faq.q3: How long does order processing take?
faq.a3: Hair in stock is shipped within 24 hours. Custom processing (clip-in, tape-in, keratin) takes 5–7 business days. Details on the Shipping page.
faq.q4: What payment methods do you accept?
faq.a4: We accept online card payment (Visa, Mastercard), bank transfer and cash on delivery. Details in the Terms & Conditions.
faq.q5: Do you ship outside Prague / internationally?
faq.a5: Yes, we deliver across the Czech Republic (Packeta) usually within 2 business days. We also offer personal delivery in Prague. Details on the Shipping page.
faq.a6: Yes, we exclusively sell 100% real natural human hair. No synthetic blends, no silicone coatings. Every bundle is from a single donor.
faq.q7: What is the difference between Virgin, Luxe and Standard?
faq.a7: Virgin = unprocessed virgin hair (highest quality), Luxe = premium Slavic hair, Standard = quality hair at an affordable price. Detailed comparison in our product range.
faq.q8: What does natural unprocessed hair mean?
faq.a8: Natural unprocessed hair is hair in its natural state — undyed, not chemically treated, with intact cuticle (outer layer). It is the most durable and longest-lasting.
faq.q9: Where does your hair come from?
faq.a9: We import hair directly from Ukraine, Belarus, Moldova and other countries. Direct import without intermediaries ensures quality and a fair price.
faq.q10: How do I know the right shade?
faq.a10: We recommend a personal consultation in Prague where we compare the shade with your hair. Online we can help via WhatsApp — send a photo in daylight.
faq.q11: What extension methods do you offer?
faq.a11: Clip-in (clips), tape-in (tape strips), keratin (keratin bonds), micro-ring (rings), weft (sew-in). Each method is suitable for a different hair type.
faq.a12: Tape-in and micro-ring are the gentlest on your own hair. Clip-in are temporary and don't stress hair at all. Keratin is the most discreet but requires heat.
faq.q13: How many grams of hair do I need?
faq.a13: It depends on your hair density and desired effect. For thickening, 50–80 g is enough, for extensions 100–150 g, for maximum volume 150–200 g. Use our weight guide.
faq.a14: Clip-in: unlimited (removable). Tape-in: 6–8 weeks (then repositioning). Keratin: 3–5 months. Micro-ring: 3–4 months. Longevity depends on care. Complete guide on the Hair Care page.
faq.q15: Can I do hair extensions at home myself?
faq.a15: You can put clip-ins on yourself in 10 minutes. Other methods (tape-in, keratin, micro-ring) should be done by a professional stylist. We can recommend a verified stylist.
faq.q16: How much do hair extensions cost?
faq.a16: The price depends on the hair category, length and weight. Complete pricing on the Hair Price List page.
faq.q17: What is included in the processing price?
faq.a17: Processing includes preparing the hair for the chosen method (cutting, attaching keratin bonds/tape strips/rings). Processing prices can be found in the price list.
faq.q18: Do you offer discounts for stylists/salons?
faq.a18: Yes, we offer B2B discounts of 15–30% off the retail price. Register as a salon or stylist for access to wholesale prices on the For Salons page.
faq.a19: We currently do not offer installment payments. Payment is available by card, bank transfer or cash on delivery.
faq.a20: Hair in stock is shipped within 24 hours. Delivery across the Czech Republic usually within 2 business days (Packeta). Personal pickup in Prague is available by arrangement.
faq.a21: Personal pickup in Prague = free. Packeta = according to current price list. Details on the Shipping page.
faq.a22: Yes, after shipping you will receive an email with a tracking number and a link to track your shipment.
faq.q23: How to care for hair extensions?
faq.a23: Proper care includes gentle washing (sulfate-free shampoo), conditioner only on lengths, brushing with a special comb from the ends, and protecting bonds from oils. Complete guide on the Hair Care page.
faq.a24: Natural and virgin hair can be dyed, but we recommend entrusting it to a professional. Dyeing may shorten the hair's lifespan. Details in the care guide.
faq.q25: How often do I need maintenance?
faq.a25: Tape-in: every 6–8 weeks. Keratin: every 3–5 months. Micro-ring: every 3–4 months. Clip-in: no maintenance needed.
faq.a26: Sulfate shampoos, silicone oils on bonds, sleeping with wet hair, aggressive brushing from roots, excessive heat without protection. Complete list in the care guide.
faq.a27: Unopened packages with an intact hygienic seal can be returned within 14 days without stating a reason. Opened hair cannot be returned for hygienic reasons. Details in the complaints policy.
faq.q28: How to file a complaint about hair?

hairCare.title: Hair extension care
hairCare.subtitle: Proper washing, brushing, nighttime routine and bond maintenance for hair extensions
hairCare.section1Title: 1. What you need to know before getting extensions
hairCare.section1Text:
Hair extensions are real human hair, but they don't grow from your head. That is the only thing you need to understand — everything else follows from it.

Your own hair receives sebum from the scalp, which continuously moisturizes and protects it. Extensions don't have this supply. From day one, they only wear down and have nothing to regenerate from. Therefore:

• external nourishment is not a luxury but a necessity — without a mask and oil, hair will inevitably dry out, lose shine and start breaking,
• heat is twice as damaging for them as for your own hair because they have no protection,
• damage is irreversible — hair cannot repair itself, once damaged it stays damaged.

Relation to complaints. This guide is also a condition for complaint acceptance. Hair damaged by insufficient care, heat styling or chemical treatment cannot be claimed (see Article A5 of the Complaints Policy). This is not a formality: the condition of the hair can be professionally assessed to distinguish a material defect from heat or chemical damage.

For stylists: pass this guide to your client during application and have them sign a handover and instruction form. Without it, you bear responsibility for non-compliance with care.
hairCare.section2Title: 2. What to do before applying extensions
hairCare.section2Text:
1. Inspect the goods — shade, length, weight, texture. Compare with the order. Anything that doesn't match, address it now, not after application. After application, shade and length can no longer be claimed.
2. Photograph the unpacked hair in daylight. A photo takes ten seconds and is your main evidence in case of a dispute.
3. Wash the hair before application with a gentle shampoo and let it air dry. This removes any shipping odor and reveals the true texture.
4. Address dyeing before application, never after, and always with a strand test first.
5. Have the hair processed and applied professionally. DIY application following internet videos is the most common cause of damage to both your own and extended hair.
6. Your own hair must be healthy. Extensions should not be applied to freshly bleached, brittle or severely damaged hair — they won't hold and will damage your natural hair.
hairCare.section3Title: 3. How to properly wash hair extensions
hairCare.section3Text:
How often: 2–3 times a week, for keratin and rings no more than every other day. Frequent washing dries out and loosens bonds. First wash no sooner than 48 hours after application to let the bonds set.

Procedure:
1. Brush hair thoroughly from ends to roots before washing. Tangled hair will matt in water.
2. Wash standing up or leaning slightly back, hair hanging freely down — never leaning forward and never in a deep sink where hair flips over and tangles.
3. Use lukewarm water, not hot. Hot water opens the cuticle and loosens keratin.
4. Apply shampoo only to roots and scalp, not along the full length. The foam that runs down during rinsing is enough to clean the ends.
5. Don't rub or twist hair between your palms. Wash with gentle top-to-bottom motions.
6. Rinse thoroughly. Shampoo residue weighs hair down and dries it out.

Which shampoo: hydrating, sulfate-free, for dry or color-treated hair. Ideally a shampoo specifically designed for hair extensions.

What to avoid: anti-dandruff shampoos, shampoos for oily hair, deep-cleansing and detox shampoos, baby shampoos, products containing salt, alcohol and sulfates (SLS, SLES). These products dissolve keratin and dry out hair.
hairCare.section4Title: 4. What nourishment do hair extensions need?
hairCare.section4Intro: This is the most commonly neglected part of care and also the most common cause of hair deterioration. Extensions without nourishment will look nice for a few weeks, with nourishment for several months. The difference is not in material quality but in care.
section4TableRow1: From mid-lengths down, never on bonds and roots
section4TableRow2: 1–2 times a week, leave on for 10–20 minutes
section4TableRow3: After every wash on damp hair
section4TableRow4: Last third of length, small amount
section4TableRow5: Along the length, away from bonds
section4TableRow6: In summer, before sun and swimming
hairCare.section4Text:
Rule for bonds: no product should be applied directly to keratin, tape or ring. Oily and oil-based ingredients loosen the bond and hair starts falling out. Always leave 2–3 cm from the bond free.

How much oil: 2–3 drops in your palm, rub between palms and run through ends. More will weigh hair down and make it greasy.

What works: argan, jojoba, macadamia oils; masks with keratin, hyaluronic acid or panthenol; protein treatment roughly once a month.

Hair vitamins and ampoules. Vitamins for extensions mean hair ampoules, serums and vitamin products applied directly to the hair, not tablets. Dietary supplements affect hair growing from your head — extensions don't grow from your head and cannot be nourished orally. Use an ampoule or vitamin serum once a week along the length, always away from bonds.

Without external nourishment it won't work. Mask, oil and ampoule are the only way to give extensions something back. Nothing can replace them.
hairCare.section5Title: 5. How to properly brush hair extensions
hairCare.section5Text:
At least twice a day — morning and evening before bed — and always before washing.

• Use a special brush for hair extensions with soft loops or a loop brush. A regular dense comb or round brush won't work with bonds.
• Brush from the bottom up: first the ends, then the middle section, finally from the roots.
• Hold hair above the bond with your free hand to avoid pulling on your own hair.
• Never brush wet hair — wet hair is at its most vulnerable. Let it at least partially dry, or use a detangling spray.
• Untangle knots with your fingers, don't pull with force.
• Don't tighten a ponytail, bun or updo at the bond area.
hairCare.section6Title: 6. How to dry and straighten hair extensions
hairCare.section6Intro:
Drying
• Gently squeeze hair in a towel after washing, don't twist or rub.
• Always dry the bonds, even if you let the rest air dry. Wet keratin and tape loosen.
• Hold the dryer at medium temperature at least 15 cm away, direct airflow from top to bottom.
• Never go to bed with wet hair.
section6TableRow4: As little as possible, ideally up to twice a week
section6TableRow5: One smooth pass, never going over the same spot
hairCare.section6Text:
Why 180 °C: above this threshold, the keratin structure of the hair begins to be irreversibly damaged. With your own hair, the damage gradually gets cut off as it grows out. Extensions don't grow — damage remains in them until they are replaced.

Hair damaged by straightening can be recognized by whitened, frayed and dry ends that matt even after washing. This condition is not a material defect and cannot be claimed.
hairCare.section7Title: 7. How to protect hair extensions during sports, in the pool and in the sun
hairCare.section7Text:
Sleep
• Always braid hair into a loose plait or twist into a loose bun above the bonds. Hair left loose tangles at the roots overnight.
• A silk or satin pillowcase significantly reduces friction and is the cheapest investment in hair longevity.
• Never sleep with wet hair. Wet bonds loosen and wet hair matts.

Sports and sweat
• Before exercising, tie hair into a ponytail or bun above the bonds.
• Sweat contains salt that dries out hair — after intense exercise, rinse hair or at least use a leave-in spray.

Pool and sea
1. Before entering the water, dampen hair with clean water and apply a protective spray or oil designed for sea and pool use (products with UV filter, beach spray for hair). Saturated and protected hair won't absorb as much chlorine and salt.
2. Tie hair up, ideally use a swim cap.
3. Rinse with clean water immediately after swimming.
4. Evening recovery: nourishing mask, then oil on ends and hair vitamins or ampoule along the length. Without this step, a day at the sea is a loss for the hair.
5. Chlorine causes a green tint in blonde hair, fading in dark hair. This condition is not a defect and cannot be claimed.

Sun and solarium
• Prolonged sun exposure dries out hair and pulls color; use a spray with UV filter or a hat.
• Always tie and cover hair in sauna and solarium.
hairCare.section8Intro: Basic rule: address dyeing before application and always with a professional stylist. DIY dyeing of extensions is the fastest way to ruin them.
section8TableRow1: Yes, carefully, by a stylist, after a strand test
hairCare.section8Text:
Why bleaching is not possible: extensions have already undergone processing and don't have the reserve that hair growing from the head has. Bleaching agents destroy the cuticle, the hair loses strength and starts breaking and tearing. This condition is irreversible.

Always test first. Before dyeing the entire set, take one strand, dye it and let it dry. Extensions absorb pigment differently than your own hair — the result is usually darker and cooler than the stylist expects.

Dyeing and complaints: any chemical treatment after receipt of the goods means the hair can no longer be claimed for texture, breakage or shade. Claim the shade before dyeing, not after.
hairCare.section9Title: 9. How often to get maintenance on hair extensions
hairCare.section9Intro: Hair extensions are not a set-and-forget thing. Your own hair grows and the bonds move away from the head — the lower they are, the more likely hair tangles in them and starts breaking.
section9TableRow5: Worn only occasionally, always remove at night
hairCare.section9Text:
Removal always by a stylist. Never pull out strands, cut them at the root or remove them with pliers at home. Improper removal damages both extended and your own hair — and is grounds for complaint rejection.

Between repositionings, have the bonds checked if you feel pulling, pricking or if knots start forming at the roots.

Break between sets. After removal, give your own hair at least 2–4 weeks of rest and intensive regenerative care before having a new set applied.
hairCare.section10Title: 10. What ruins hair extensions the fastest?
hairCare.section10Text:
Print this list and put it on your fridge.

1. Straightening without heat protection or above 180 °C.
2. No mask or oil. Hair without nourishment dries out within a few weeks.
3. Bleaching and highlighting. Irreversible damage in a single visit.
4. Sleeping with loose or wet hair.
5. Shampoo with sulfates, anti-dandruff or for oily hair.
6. Applying mask and oil to bonds. Bonds loosen and hair starts falling out.
7. Not brushing. A matted pad at the roots can no longer be combed out.
8. Brushing wet hair or with a coarse comb.
9. Pool and sea without protection.
10. Delaying repositioning. Bonds slide down, tangle and pull out your own hair.

Summary in one sentence: heat down, nourishment up, leave bonds alone, brush twice a day.

advice.typy_prodlouzeni_content:
Main extension methods: clip-in (clips, occasional wear), tape-in (tapes, 6–8 weeks), keratin (most durable, 3–5 months) and micro ring (rings, no adhesive). Each is suitable for different hair types and lifestyles.

Detailed method comparisons can be found on our blog: clip-in vs tape-in vs keratin and keratin vs micro ring.
advice.clip_in_vs_tape_in_content:
Clip-in strands can be attached by yourself in a few minutes — ideal for occasional wear. Tape-in tapes are applied by a stylist and last 6–8 weeks — comfortable for everyday wear. Both methods are gentle on your own hair.

A detailed comparison of all methods including keratin extensions can be found in our blog article.
advice.jak_vybrat_barvu_content:
When choosing a color, match the shade at the roots, not the bleached tips. Compare in daylight and if you are hesitating between two shades, choose the darker one. Not sure? Arrange a personal consultation — we will come with hair samples directly to you.

Also read about the most common mistakes when choosing hair color to avoid.
advice.jak_vybrat_delku_content:
The most popular length is 50–55 cm (below the shoulder blades). For fine hair, we recommend max. 55 cm. We measure the length from the attachment point, not from the top of the head — the longer the extension, the more it weighs on your own hair.

A complete guide to choosing hair (color, length, quality, amount) can be found on our blog.
advice.pece_o_prodlouzene_vlasy_content:
Brush hair from tips upward, braid before sleeping and wash with sulfate-free shampoo. Do not use conditioner on bonds and avoid contact with adhesive or rings when styling.

A detailed care guide (washing, drying, night routine, bond maintenance) can be found on our blog.
advice.puvod_vlasu_content:
Hair structure varies by origin. Ukrainian and Russian hair is the most sought after in Europe — fine, silky, with a natural range of shades. Kazakh hair has a stronger structure, Turkish hair is more affordable.

Why is Ukrainian hair considered the highest quality? Read in our detailed article.
advice.virgin_vs_remy_content:
What is virgin hair?

Virgin hair is completely natural — never dyed, bleached or chemically treated. It is hair in its purest form, with an intact cuticle. It has the longest lifespan and the most natural shine.

What is remy hair?

Remy hair has the cuticle aligned in one direction (from root to tip). It may be lightly treated or dyed, but retains the natural fiber direction. This prevents tangling.

Which type to choose?

  • Virgin — highest quality, longest lifespan, higher price. Ideal for keratin and tape-in extensions.
  • Remy — excellent quality at a more affordable price. Suitable for all extension methods.
advice.jak_dlouho_vydrzi_content:
Lifespan by method

Clip-in: with proper care 1–2 years. Depends on wearing frequency.

Tape-in: tapes last 6–8 weeks, the hair itself can be re-taped 2–3 times.

Keratin: bond lasts 3–5 months. Hair can be reapplied.

Micro ring: 2–4 months between maintenance. Hair can be repositioned.

What affects lifespan

  • Hair quality — virgin and remy last longer than standard.
  • Care — proper washing, brushing and styling extend lifespan.
  • Heat styling frequency — less flat ironing = longer lifespan.
  • Your own hair type — oily hair may shorten the lifespan of bonded attachments.

weightGuide.title: How many grams of hair do I need?
weightGuide.metaTitle: Hair weight calculator — how many grams do I need
weightGuide.metaDesc: How many grams of hair do I need? Weight calculator — enter length, density and method. Recommends weight and price. Free consultation.
weightGuide.subtitle: The right weight is key to a natural result. It depends on your hair type, desired volume and processing method.
weightGuide.guideTitle: How many grams of hair do I need by effect?
weightGuide.guideIntro: Hair weight is measured in grams and determines the total volume of extensions. The more grams, the fuller and richer the result. Every woman is different — it depends on your own hair density, desired length and processing method.
weightGuide.g100desc: Adds volume and slightly extends. Ideal for fine hair or those who want a subtle change. Suitable for shorter extensions up to 40 cm.
weightGuide.g150desc: The most popular choice. Significantly adds volume and naturally extends hair. Suitable for normal hair and lengths of 40–50 cm.
weightGuide.g200desc: 200 g of hair for thick hair or extensions 50+ cm.
weightGuide.g250desc: 250+ g for extensions 60+ cm or very thick hair.
weightGuide.hairTypeTitle: How many grams do I need based on my hair type?
weightGuide.hairTypeIntro: Your own hair type is the most important factor when choosing weight. Fine hair requires fewer grams, thick hair requires more.
weightGuide.typeFineNote: Fine hair does not need as many grams for a visible effect. A smaller amount prevents overloading your own hair and the extensions will look natural.
weightGuide.typeNormalNote: 150–200 g for normal hair. The most commonly ordered weight.
weightGuide.typeThickNote: Thick hair needs more grams so that the extensions visually blend with your own volume. Otherwise the transition would be visible.
weightGuide.processingTitle: How many grams do I need for clip-in vs. tape-in?
weightGuide.processingIntro: The processing method affects how many grams you will need for the same visual effect.
weightGuide.clipInDesc: Clip-in hair is attached with clips and usually requires 20–30% more grams for a full effect, because it is concentrated in fewer strands. The advantage is easy application and the option to remove daily. For a full effect on normal hair, expect 180–220 g.
weightGuide.tapeInDesc: Tape-in hair is distributed more evenly across the entire head, so fewer grams are needed for the same visual effect. Application is done by a stylist and lasts 6–8 weeks before re-taping. For normal hair, 120–160 g is sufficient.
weightGuide.faqTitle: Most frequently asked questions about hair weight
weightGuide.faq1q: How many grams do I need for a full head?
weightGuide.faq1a: For a full head, it depends on your hair density. Fine hair: 100–150 g, normal: 150–200 g, thick: 200–250+ g. Most clients choose 150 g for a natural result.
weightGuide.faq2a: 100 g is enough for subtle volume enhancement or for fine hair. For significant lengthening or full volume, we recommend 150 g or more.
weightGuide.faq3q: What is the difference in weight between clip-in and tape-in?
weightGuide.faq3a: Clip-in hair requires 20–30% more grams than tape-in for the same effect. Tape-in distributes more evenly, so less material is needed.
weightGuide.faq4a: Price is directly proportional to weight — 200 g costs twice as much as 100 g of the same hair type. That is why it is important to choose the right amount and not waste.
weightGuide.faq5q: Can I purchase more hair later?
weightGuide.faq5a: Yes, you can purchase additional hair of the same type and color at any time. However, we recommend ordering a sufficient amount at once, as shades may vary slightly between batches.
weightGuide.faq6q: How many grams for a short extension (10–20 cm)?
weightGuide.faq6a: For a short extension of 10–20 cm, fewer grams are needed — for fine hair 80–100 g, for normal 100–130 g. The shorter the extension, the less material you need.
weightGuide.faq7q: How many grams of hair do I need for a 20 cm extension?
weightGuide.faq7a: For a 20 cm extension, you need approximately 120–160 g depending on your hair density and chosen method. Fine hair: 100–120 g, normal: 120–150 g, thick: 150–180 g. Use our weight calculator for an exact calculation.
